Add the `imbue-mngr-witness` package (`libs/mngr_witness`): the behavior-corpus witness pipeline designed in `specs/behaviors-mapreduce/spec.md`, run as `mngr witness`. It depends on `imbue-mngr-mapreduce` for the declarative pipeline model and its executor, and on `imbue-mngr-behaviors` for corpus parsing; it does not depend on `imbue-mngr-tmr`.

`pipeline.py` builds the witness instance of the declarative model: five nodes (setup, map, review, integrate, reduce) with their fan-outs, the artifacts each needs and produces, their gates, and the prompt templates their agents receive. `specs/behaviors-mapreduce/pipeline.svg` is rendered from the packaged default and a drift test fails when the picture no longer matches the model.

`prompts.py` and `prompt_assets/` hold the four node templates (`scaffold.j2`, `mapper.j2`, `reviewer.j2`, `annealer.j2`) and the partials they include, carried by the pipeline as its template family. A project fills their blocks by `{% extends %}` from `<project>/witness/<name>.j2`. The prompts state the read-only corpus, the `[KIND]` commit convention, the clause trace and the positively defined verdicts, the evidence each node ships, and each node's outcome schema rendered from the same models the gates parse. Sections that list units, existing witnesses, or branches are rendered by the bindings into the string variables the templates place.

`outcomes.py` holds those models (`SetupOutcome`, `MapperOutcome`, `ReviewOutcome`, `ReduceOutcome`, the `UnitRecord` with its verdict and clause trace) and the loaders for an agent's archive, including the `witness_links.jsonl` back-links and the `junit.xml` report. `clauses.py` lists the clauses a unit's trace must name (a Rule's name, or a scenario's `Then` steps and their `And`/`But` continuations). `corpus.py` scans a validated corpus into one `FeatureTask` per feature file, each with an agent-name-safe slug, narrowed by `--feature`, `--area`, `--tag`, and `--unit`.

`gates.py` holds the nine mechanical gates the executor runs on every published job: corpus untouched, ruff clean, commit kinds confined to their paths, no changelog before the reduce node and exactly one after it, every assigned unit reported, every witness link resolvable, junit present and consistent, and every verdict backed by a trace that names a real clause. A job that committed nothing passes the diff gates and is judged on its archive. `conventions.py` holds the layout rules the gates and prompts share. `bindings.py` binds the nodes: the scaffold job, one mapper job per feature file, one reviewer job per successful mapper (a mapper that committed nothing is still reviewed, from where it started), the orchestrator's cherry-pick of reviewed work onto `<pipeline>/<execution>/integrate/integration`, and the annealer job whose branch `<pipeline>/<execution>/reduce/integrated` is the deliverable. `gitops.py` holds the git helpers the gates and bindings share.

`plan.py` builds the `ExecutionPlan` from the command line (`--provider`, `--node-provider reduce=local`, `--node-env reduce:KEY=VALUE`, `--max-running-agents`, `--timeout`, `--keep-hosts`). `agent_type.py` registers `witness-claude`, a plugin-provided agent type that is claude with permission prompts and startup dialogs switched off, so no agent pauses for approval and the operator edits no config; it is the default `--agent-type`, and the command warns when another type may pause.

`cli.py` registers `mngr witness`, which validates the corpus, builds the pipeline for the project's prompt variants, the plan, and the bindings, runs the executor, and writes `execution.json` under the output directory. `mock_witness_test.py` plays all five nodes in-process against a scripted executor, and `test_witness_pipeline.py` runs the whole pipeline end to end.

`mngr witness` replaces `mngr tmr-behaviors`, which is removed in the same change; the `behaviors` corpora of `libs/mngr_forward`, `apps/minds`, and `libs/mngr_claude` carry their prompt variants under `<project>/witness/`.

- The exhaustiveness guard in `clauses.py` carries a `pragma: no cover` so the package's 100 percent coverage gate holds under CI's plain `coverage report`, which applies only the default exclusions.
